Maya: FYI — EdiCorp says they started seeing 429s during a load spike while running their internal smoke test (~14:10 UTC). They report errors after ~25-40s of sustained parallel requests.
Kevin: Which endpoint and are they using streaming?
Maya: /v1/complete, streaming enabled, single API key. They included the X-RateLimit headers in their screenshots: x-ratelimit-limit: 180, x-ratelimit-remaining: 0, x-ratelimit-reset: 22. Body was `{'error':'Rate limit exceeded'}`.
Sam: Pulled logs for that key — saw a spike where request concurrency jumped from 12 -> 92 over ~10s, token emission also jumped (many long prompts). 429s line up with token-window exhaustion.
Iris: Sounds like TPM token-bucket hit rather than pure RPM. They might be testing with short delays between requests so burst bucket drained fast. Do we know their tokens-per-request distribution?
Maya: They said avg prompt ~800 tokens, responses ~1200 tokens. Test harness: `hey -n 1200 -c 40 -m POST -D body.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/complete` run over ~90s with a scripted ramp.
Kevin: Repro plan for infra: 1) spawn staging key mapped to same quota config 2) run `wrk -t8 -c40 -d60s --script=streaming.lua` that emits payloads matching 800/1200 token mix 3) capture x-ratelimit headers and per-second token rate.
ops-bot: started replay job id=rl-replay-1719876430 profile=spike-40c prompt_size=800 resp_size=1200 ETA=3m
Sam: Quick heuristic I'd suggest for "sane defaults" (non-enterprise keys): 120 RPM (requests), 60k TPM (tokens), burst_capacity: 2x token-bucket for 10s. That gives headroom for short spikes but protects backend.
Iris: For infra knobs to check: `rate_window_seconds=60`, `burst_window_seconds=10`, `burst_multiplier=2.0-3.0` depending on model heavy tokens. Also ensure streaming flush doesn't count double tokens.
Kevin: If customers use streaming and long responses, count tokens on generation side. TPM should reflect generated + prompt tokens. Also verify our sliding-window implementation vs fixed-window; sliding is more forgiving for sub-minute bursts.
Maya: I'll send repro steps to EdiCorp and ask them to run the exact `wrk` script and share `X-RateLimit-*` headers. Also asked them for raw prompt sizes.
Sam: For internal benchmarking we should add a new profile to loadlab: `spike-longresponse-40c` (800/1200 token mix, 40 concurrent, 1m runs). Collect pct95 latency and 429 onset time.
Iris: Ops action: Kevin, can you run the staging repro and post the short run results (headers + rate curves)? I'll check limiter config and whether burst token replenishment is tuned correctly for streaming workloads.
Kevin: On it. Spinning up staging run now — will post results in ~4m.
Maya: Thanks everyone — I'll keep customer updated with timeline. If we need to raise their quota as short-term mitigation, I'll coord with Billing after we confirm repro. :thumbsup:
Kevin: result snippet (from staging): `x-ratelimit-limit: 180, x-ratelimit-remaining: 0, x-ratelimit-reset: 18` right when 429s started. Token/sec hit ~3.2k during spike.
Sam: Noted — that aligns with bucket exhaustion. After we run more profiles we'll propose default quotas and an FAQ blurb for support on how to interpret 429 vs quota-breach. :eyes:
